restatement: Make template size bounded. A new limit, limits.maxNodes (default 20000), counts every AST node except the Program root while parsing, parent before children, at each node's opening token. Node maxNodes + 1 fails with a limit-nodes diagnostic at that node, with the same code and position in render, validate, analyze and resolveTemplate. Long ELSEIF chains and deep nesting must end in a result or a coded diagnostic, never a stack overflow. The API accepts options.limits.maxNodes but may only lower it, and validate and analyze on the server use the server's maxNodes. The CLI gets --max-nodes, and the OpenAPI Limits and RequestLimits schemas list the field. analyze uses the caller's limits and otherwise the defaults; with no caller maxDepth it stops failing beyond 32 levels and bounds only absurd nesting. Existing test expectations (apart from the named default-limits fixtures) and existing outputs stay unchanged, with no new runtime dependency and no eval.
brief_mismatch: Section 1's must-nots and card.md's must-nots disagree. The card lists 'change any existing test expectation other than the one named amendment (if any)' (only spec.test.ts in its interface contract), 'compile a template-supplied regular expression' and 'let an unknown name or bad parameter pass in lenient mode (ADR 0003)'. Contract m1 names three fixture amendments (spec.test.ts, limits.test.ts, api.test.ts), and m2 ('change what any existing template outputs') does not appear in the card. spec.md Decisions resolve the fixture list, but the card text was never brought into line. I reviewed against section 1.
